name: Epstein-Barr virus-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
aliases: Epstein-Barr virus-associated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016)

criteria.description: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma morphology on histopathological examination
Detection of Epstein-Barr virus in tumor cells by EBER in situ hybridization
Expression of B-cell markers (CD20, CD79a) with variable expression of activation markers
Presence of rapidly enlarging lymphadenopathy or extranodal mass

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with EBV positivity in tumor cells by EBER in situ hybridization and immunophenotyping confirming B-cell lineage
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other EBV-associated lymphoproliferative disorders.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically involves cervical, mediastinal, or abdominal lymph nodes
searchTerms: fast growing painless swollen lymph nodes

pathognomonic.symptomName: EBV-encoded RNA (EBER) positivity in tumor cells
pathognomonic.notes: Detected by in situ hybridization; diagnostic hallmark

common.symptomName: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)

common.notes: Commonly involves gastrointestinal tract, skin, or lungs
May be present due to marrow involvement or systemic inflammation
searchTerms: low red blood cells from chronic illness
chronic disease causing low blood count

occasional.symptomName: Dyspnea due to mediastinal mass effect
searchTerms: shortness of breath from chest mass
breathing difficulty due to mediastinal tumor

rare.notes: Rare but associated with poor prognosis

searchTerms: immune system attacks related to cancer

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to tumor infiltration

laboratory: Positive EBER in situ hybridization in tumor cells
imaging: CT or PET-CT showing bulky lymphadenopathy and extranodal masses
MRI for CNS involvement if suspected
genetic: Absence of MYC rearrangement distinguishes from Burkitt lymphoma
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, CD79a, and variable CD30

distinguishingFeatures: CD15 and CD30 positivity with absence of EBER in most cases
Typically EBV positive in endemic cases but distinct morphology
Often EBV positive but clinical context differs

redFlags: Rapidly progressive lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms
Neurological deficits suggestive of CNS involvement
Unexplained severe cytopenias or organ dysfunction
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2016.
Oyama T, Ichimura K, Suzuki R, et al. Age-related EBV-associated B-cell lymphoproliferative disorders: a clinicopathologic study of 96 patients. Blood. 2003;101(4): 1505-1512.
Orphanet: Epstein-Barr virus-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (ORPHA:289661)
